formation.title: The Birth of Slovakia
formation.text:
From the mist-shrouded peaks of the Carpathians to the gold-rich valleys of the Ore Mountains, a new nation stirs. For centuries, the Slovak people have been the miners, shepherds, and soldiers of Upper Hungary: their silver funded empires, their fortresses held the mountain passes, their towns grew wealthy on copper and coin. Now, as Slovakia stands on its own, a choice presents itself: shall we build upon the wealth beneath our mountains, or upon the strength of the passes that guard them?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are the Mining Crown of the Carpathians

modifiers.name: Mining Crown of the Carpathians
modifiers.text: Slovakia's mineral wealth (silver from Banska Stiavnica, gold from Kremnica, copper from Banska Bystrica) forms the bedrock of a new national prosperity. Technical innovation in the mines drives institutional advancement.

options.text: We are the Frontier Bastion of Christendom

modifiers.name: Frontier Bastion of Christendom
modifiers.text: Guarding the Carpathian passes against Ottoman and steppe raiders, Slovakia's fortress tradition and mountain militias form the shield of Central Europe. Every valley is a deathtrap for invaders.

advances.name: Carpathian Mountain Defense
advances.text: The mountain passes of the Carpathians are Slovakia's natural fortress. Local militias (the Horali) patrol the ridgelines, and watchtowers dot the high ground, providing early warning against raids from any direction.

advances.name: Royal Mining Privileges
advances.text: Hungarian kings grant extensive mining privileges to the towns of the Slovak Ore Mountains, attracting German settlers and establishing the legal framework for Europe's most productive silver and copper mines.

advances.name: Valasi Pastoral Tradition
advances.text: Vlach shepherds migrate into the Carpathian highlands, bringing with them a distinctive pastoral economy centered on sheep herding, bryndza cheese-making, and seasonal transhumance across the mountain meadows.

advances.name: Royal Charter Towns
advances.text: Mining settlements like Kremnica, Banska Stiavnica, and Banska Bystrica receive royal charters granting them German town law, self-governance, and trading privileges that drive urban development.

advances.name: Carpathian Religious Mosaic
advances.text: Catholic, Orthodox, and later Protestant communities coexist in the Carpathian borderlands, where the practical demands of mountain life foster a tradition of religious pragmatism.

advances.name: Castle Building Tradition
advances.text: The great castles of Spis, Orava, and Trencin dominate the Slovak landscape: massive stone fortifications built to control mountain passes and river crossings, forming an integrated defensive network.

advances.name: Valasi Shepherd Cavalry
advances.text: The mounted shepherds of the Carpathian highlands serve as light cavalry, their intimate knowledge of mountain terrain making them invaluable as scouts and raiders in the rugged country along the frontier.

advances.name: Kremnica Minting Tradition
advances.text: The Kremnica mint, founded in 1328, produces the famous golden ducats that circulate across Europe. Its precise coinage standards and technical expertise make it one of the most respected mints in Christendom.

advances.name: Thurzo-Fugger Enterprise
advances.text: The partnership between Jan Thurzo and Jakob Fugger creates the largest copper-producing enterprise in the world, processing nearly forty percent of global output from the mines around Banska Bystrica.

event.title: The Thurzo-Fugger Partnership
event.text: The partnership between the Slovak noble Jan Thurzo and the Augsburg merchant Jakob Fugger has created the mightiest copper enterprise in Europe. Their mines in Banska Bystrica produce nearly half the world's copper, their smelters blaze day and night, and their trading networks stretch from Venice to the Levant. How shall we profit from this extraordinary wealth?

modifiers.name: Thurzo-Fugger Monopoly
modifiers.text: The Thurzo-Fugger enterprise holds exclusive rights to Slovak copper and silver. Their capital and expertise drive production to unprecedented levels.

modifiers.name: Mining Guilds Charter
modifiers.text: Independent mining guilds compete freely in the Slovak Ore Mountains, building infrastructure and recruiting skilled miners from across Central Europe.

advances.name: Highland Textile Tradition
advances.text:
Vlach pastoral communities in the Carpathian highlands develop a tradition of wool processing, producing coarse cloth and felt from their mountain sheep flocks for trade in lowland markets.

Available in: Salas

advances.name: Mining Technology
advances.text: Slovak miners pioneer water drainage systems, ventilation shafts, and ore-processing techniques that push mines deeper than ever before, maintaining productivity even as surface deposits are exhausted.

advances.name: Hungarian Military Service
advances.text: Slovak soldiers serve in Hungarian royal armies, gaining experience in the frontier wars and developing a reputation as reliable infantry in the campaigns against Ottoman expansion.

advances.name: Banska Town Guard
advances.text: The wealthy mining towns of the Slovak Ore Mountains maintain professional guards trained in pike and shot tactics, defending their silver and copper from bandits, raiders, and Ottoman incursions.

advances.name: Coronation City of Pressburg
advances.text: After the fall of Buda to the Ottomans in 1541, Bratislava becomes the coronation city of Hungarian kings. For over two centuries, eleven monarchs are crowned in St. Martin's Cathedral.

event.title: Coronation City of Pressburg
event.text: With the fall of Buda to the Ottomans, Pressburg (known to the Slovaks as Bratislava) has become the coronation city of the Hungarian kings. St. Martin's Cathedral now witnesses the crowning of monarchs, the Diet convenes within our walls, and the archbishop makes his seat here. Pressburg has become the de facto capital of a kingdom. How shall we leverage this extraordinary elevation?

options.text: Let the coronations enhance our prestige

modifiers.name: Coronation City Prestige
modifiers.text: As the seat of royal coronations and the Hungarian Diet, Pressburg commands the respect of European courts and enhances Slovakia's diplomatic standing.

options.text: Develop Pressburg as a commercial hub

modifiers.name: Pressburg Commerce
modifiers.text: Pressburg's position on the Danube, combined with its new status as a political capital, makes it a natural center for trade between Vienna, Buda, and the East.

advances.name: Ottoman Frontier Defense
advances.text: Southern Slovakia becomes a battleground as Ottoman forces push northward after Mohacs. Fortified towns and castle garrisons form a defensive line protecting the mining regions from Turkish raids.

advances.name: Upper Hungary as Refuge
advances.text:
As central Hungary falls under Ottoman occupation, refugees flood northward into Slovakia: nobles, burghers, scholars, and craftsmen who enrich the cultural and economic life of Upper Hungary.

Available in: Salas

advances.name: Advanced Ore Smelting
advances.text:
New smelting techniques developed in the Slovak mining towns extract higher yields from copper and iron ore, producing tools and implements that are traded across Central Europe.

Available in: Banska Mining Works

advances.name: University of Trnava
advances.text: Founded by Jesuits in 1635, the University of Trnava becomes the premier institution of higher learning in Upper Hungary, educating a generation of clergy, lawyers, and administrators.

advances.name: Kuruc Revolt
advances.text: The dispossessed Protestant nobles of Upper Hungary rise as Kuruci, waging guerrilla warfare through the Carpathian valleys. Their foot, the Talpasi, are raised among the Slovak and Rusyn villagers of the northern counties, and Slovak soldiers on both sides gain hard-won experience in mountain combat.

event.title: The Kuruc Uprising
event.text: The dispossessed nobles and Protestant fighters of Upper Hungary have taken up arms as Kuruci, rebels against Habsburg domination. Led by charismatic commanders, they wage guerrilla warfare through the Carpathian valleys, burning and raiding. The Slovak lands are torn between those who join the rebellion and those who seek accommodation with Vienna. Which path serves our interests?

modifiers.name: Spirit of the Kuruci
modifiers.text: The fighting spirit of the Kuruc rebels inspires Slovak soldiers. Their guerrilla tactics in the Carpathian valleys prove devastatingly effective against conventional armies.

modifiers.name: Habsburg Accommodation
modifiers.text: By seeking pragmatic terms with Vienna, Slovakia secures religious tolerance and administrative privileges that ensure stability and diplomatic standing.

advances.name: Reformation in the Mining Towns
advances.text: Lutheran and Calvinist preachers find fertile ground in Slovakia's mining towns, where literate German and Slovak burghers embrace the new faith, founding schools and printing presses.

advances.name: Carpathian Commerce
advances.text:
Slovakia's dual economy matures: highland shepherds produce bryndza and wool for market, while the mining towns mint ducats and trade copper ingots across Europe.

Available in: Salas

advances.name: Counter-Reformation
advances.text:
Habsburg-sponsored Catholic revival brings Jesuit missions, new churches, and renewed religious authority to Slovakia. The restored faith commissions sacred jewelry and liturgical art from Kremnica's goldsmiths.

Available in: Kremnica Mint

advances.name: Thokoly's Kingdom
advances.text: Imre Thokoly's brief Kingdom of Upper Hungary demonstrates that Slovak territory can serve as a power base independent of both Vienna and Constantinople, inspiring future generations.

advances.name: Arms Manufacture
advances.text:
The iron forges and copper smelters of the Slovak mining districts begin producing weapons and armor, supplying the frontier garrisons fighting on the Ottoman border.

Available in: Banska Mining Works

advances.name: Banska Stiavnica Mining Academy
advances.text: Founded in 1735 and elevated to a royal academy under Maria Theresa, the Mining Academy of Banska Stiavnica becomes the world's first institution of technical higher education, training engineers and mineralogists.

advances.name: Professional Regiments
advances.text: Under Habsburg military reforms, Slovak districts raise professional infantry regiments (the Toborsek) trained in linear tactics and equipped with modern firearms.

advances.name: Theresian Reforms
advances.text: Maria Theresa's administrative reforms bring centralized governance, standardized taxation, and systematic mineral surveys to Upper Hungary. Her consort Francis of Lorraine turns his estate at Holic into a model of the new economy: the majolica works he founds there in 1743 is the first in the kingdom.

advances.name: Iron Industry
advances.text:
The ironworks of the Slovak mining districts expand from raw smelting to steel production, supplying the growing Habsburg military and industrial demand.

Available in: Banska Mining Works

advances.name: Technical Education
advances.text: The mining school teaches mathematics, mechanics, hydraulics and surveying, and its masters put the lessons to work in the hills. Samuel Mikoviny, its first professor, lays out the tajchy: reservoirs whose water drives the pumps that keep the deep shafts dry.

advances.name: Industrial Foundations
advances.text: Timber processing, ironworks, and glass manufacturing expand across the Slovak valleys, laying the foundations for industrial development beyond traditional mining.

advances.name: Slovak National Awakening
advances.text: Ludovit Stur's codification of standard Slovak in 1843 ignites a national cultural movement. Newspapers, literature, and education in the Slovak language forge a common identity from Bratislava to Kosice.

event.title: The Voice of a Nation
event.text: Ludovit Stur has accomplished what centuries of shared suffering could not: he has given the Slovak people a common language. Meeting at Hlboke in 1843, Stur and his companions Hodza and Hurban have codified standard Slovak based on the Central Slovak dialect. For the first time, Slovaks from Bratislava to Kosice can read the same newspapers, sing the same songs, and dream the same dreams. The Matica Slovenska stands ready to carry this new language to every village in the Carpathians.

modifiers.name: The Slovak National Language
modifiers.text: The codification of standard Slovak by Ludovit Stur creates a common cultural identity, spurring literacy, cultural production, and national pride across the Slovak lands.

advances.name: Matica Slovenska
advances.text: The Matica Slovenska, founded in 1863, becomes the institutional heart of Slovak cultural life: promoting literature, education, and the standard language across the Carpathian region.

advances.name: Slovak Volunteer Corps
advances.text: In the revolutionary year of 1848, Slovak volunteers led by Stur, Hodza, and Hurban take up arms for national rights, fighting for recognition against Hungarian revolutionary forces.

advances.name: Peasant Emancipation
advances.text: The abolition of serfdom frees the Slovak peasantry, unlocking population growth and economic mobility as former serfs enter the urban workforce and expand agricultural production.

advances.name: Mining Industrialization
advances.text: Steam engines, rail transport, and modern mining techniques transform Slovakia's ancient mining industry, increasing production and connecting the Ore Mountains to European markets.

advances.name: Pan-Slavic Congress
advances.text: Slovak delegates at the Pan-Slavic Congress of 1848 forge connections with Czech, Polish, Serbian, and other Slavic movements, building diplomatic networks that strengthen Slovakia's position.

destiny.name: The Carpathian Crossroads
destiny.text: Slovakia stands at the crossroads of Central Europe. Rich in minerals and guarded by mountain passes, this young nation must choose its path: will it be known for the wealth beneath its peaks, or the strength of the walls that guard them?

event.title: The Carpathian Crossroads
event.text: The formation of Slovakia has placed a new power at the heart of Central Europe. The Carpathian Mountains define our nation: rich with silver and copper beneath their peaks, and impassable to any army that does not know their passes. Our path forward is marked by the choices we made at the founding. Now we must walk that path to its conclusion.

options.text: Our destiny awaits in the mountains

destiny.name: Masters of the Ore Mountains
destiny.text: Extend Slovak mining control beyond the homeland into the mineral-rich Silesian borderlands. Control of Krnov and Fryvaldov brings new silver and gold deposits under our administration.

conditions.text: Own Krnov, or a subject owns it
Own Frývaldov, or a subject owns it

event.title: Masters of the Ore Mountains
event.text: Our miners have pushed beyond the homeland, bringing the mineral-rich borderlands of Silesia under Slovak administration. The ancient mining traditions of the Ore Mountains (water pumps, ventilation shafts, advanced smelting) now serve a greater enterprise. From Kremnica to Krnov, Slovak mining expertise sets the standard for Central Europe.

options.text: The mountains yield their treasures to us

destiny.name: The Silver Road
destiny.text: The Thurzo-Fugger partnership showed how Slovak metals could reach European markets. Secure the trade route to Augsburg and raise the mining works at Banska Bystrica, where the partners smelted the copper they sold across Europe.

conditions.text: Own Augsburg, or a subject owns it
We own Banska Bystrica and it has Banska Mining Works

event.title: The Silver Road
event.text: Slovak silver and copper flow along the trade routes to Augsburg, the financial heart of Europe. The old Thurzo-Fugger partnership has been succeeded by a network of commercial relationships that span the continent. Our metals fund armies and build cathedrals from Lisbon to Constantinople. How shall we organize this extraordinary commerce?

modifiers.name: Fugger Trade Network
modifiers.text: Slovak metals flow through the Fugger trade network to markets across Europe. The commercial connections forged by this partnership enhance both wealth and diplomatic standing.

modifiers.name: Royal Mint Monopoly
modifiers.text: The crown exercises exclusive control over Slovak minting and precious metal production. Royal coinage circulates at fixed standards, stabilizing the currency and strengthening crown authority.

destiny.name: Academia Montanistica
destiny.text: Transform Slovakia into Europe's center of mining science. Control the great trade cities of Nuremberg and Wroclaw, build up Kremnica, the town of the mint and of the chamber counts, and let the Bergamt administer a mineral empire.

conditions.text: Own Nuremberg, or a subject owns it
Own Wrocław, or a subject owns it
We own Kremnica and its development is at least 30

event.title: Academia Montanistica
event.text: The Mining Academy of Banska Stiavnica has grown into the foremost institution of technical education in Europe. Its graduates (engineers, mineralogists, metallurgists) carry Slovak mining science to every corner of the continent. The Bergamt, our royal mining administration, coordinates a mineral empire stretching from Nuremberg to Wroclaw. This is the apex of Slovak technical civilization.

modifiers.name: Mining Revolution
modifiers.text: Slovak mining science has transformed the extraction industry. Steam-powered pumps, precision surveying, and advanced metallurgy make our mines the most productive and innovative in Europe.

options.text: Let our treasury overflow with gold

modifiers.name: Golden Treasury
modifiers.text: The accumulated mineral wealth of the Carpathians fills Slovak coffers. This golden treasury funds reconstruction, diplomacy, and territorial consolidation.

destiny.name: Guardians of the Passes
destiny.text: Secure the southern approaches by taking Eger and Miskolc. These fortress towns guard the gateway between the Hungarian plain and the Carpathian highlands. In Slovak hands, they seal the mountain wall.

conditions.text: Own Eger, or a subject owns it
Own Miskolc, or a subject owns it

event.title: Guardians of the Passes
event.text: The fortress towns of Eger and Miskolc now fly the Slovak banner. These ancient strongholds guard the gateway between the Hungarian plain and the Carpathian highlands. With their walls under our command, the southern approaches to Slovakia are sealed. No army can march north through these passes without facing our garrisons.

destiny.name: Antemurale Christianitatis
destiny.text: Slovakia claims the ancient title of Bulwark of Christendom. Take Buda itself and raise an army worthy of this sacred duty.

conditions.text: Own Buda, or a subject owns it

event.title: Antemurale Christianitatis
event.text: With the capture of Buda, Slovakia has proven itself the shield of Central Europe. Our army, trained in the mountain warfare traditions of the Carpathians, has reclaimed the ancient seat of the Hungarian kings. The title of Antemurale Christianitatis (Bulwark of Christendom) belongs to us by right of arms. How shall we consolidate this sacred duty?

options.text: Train our soldiers in mountain warfare

modifiers.name: Mountain Warfare Doctrine
modifiers.text: Slovak soldiers are trained in the art of mountain combat: ambush, guerrilla raids, and the use of terrain to negate numerical superiority. Our raiding parties strip enemy supply lines bare, though maintaining these scattered mountain garrisons strains the treasury.

modifiers.name: Integrated Garrison Network
modifiers.text: A coordinated system of fortified towns, watchtower chains, and garrison forces maintains control across the Carpathian frontier. Every pass is watched, every valley patrolled, though the inward military focus slows integration of new territories.

destiny.name: The Carpathian Wall
destiny.text: From Vienna to Belgrade, the Carpathian defensive line is complete. Slovakia commands the mountain fortress system that shields all of Central Europe, and Pressburg, the capital behind the wall, is built up as the seat of crown and diet.

conditions.text: Own Belgrad, or a subject owns it
Own Wien, or a subject owns it
We own Pressburg and its development is at least 52

event.title: The Carpathian Wall
event.text: From Vienna to Belgrade, the Carpathian defensive line is complete. Slovak fortresses command every mountain pass, river crossing, and strategic valley. Our garrison network is the most formidable defensive system in Europe. Armies that enter the Carpathians do not leave. Slovakia has become the immovable shield at the heart of the continent.

modifiers.name: The Unconquerable
modifiers.text: Slovakia's mountain fortress network is legendary. No invading army has successfully conquered the Carpathian wall, and the reputation of Slovak military strength commands respect at the negotiating table, though this martial confidence breeds complacency at court.

modifiers.name: Crusader Spirit
modifiers.text: Slovakia fights with the fervor of a holy cause. As the Bulwark of Christendom, every war is a crusade, every soldier a defender of the faith.

units.name: Horali
units.text: Carpathian mountain militia drawn from highland villages. Expert ambushers who know every pass, ravine, and ridgeline in the Slovak mountains.

units.name: Valasi Riders
units.text: Mounted Vlach shepherds from the Carpathian highlands. Tough, mobile, and accustomed to operating independently in the most forbidding mountain terrain.

units.name: Talpasi
units.text: The foot of the Kuruc risings, raised among the Slovak and Rusyn villagers of Upper Hungary. Quick to gather and to strike in the valleys, unsteady in a pitched battle.

units.name: Slovak Volunteers
units.text: Students, craftsmen and villagers who answered the call of Hurban, Stur and Hodza in 1848. Ardent, and armed with whatever was to hand.

units.name: Banska Guard
units.text: Professional town guards from the wealthy mining towns of the Slovak Ore Mountains. Well-equipped and disciplined, they defend the silver and copper that funds the kingdom.

units.name: Toborsek
units.text: Professional infantry regiments raised from the Slovak mining districts under Habsburg military reforms. Trained in linear warfare and equipped with modern arms.

buildings.name: Banska Mining Works
buildings.text: Industrial mining infrastructure in the Slovak Ore Mountains, exploiting rich deposits of silver, copper, and other metals using advanced drainage and smelting techniques.

children.text: The location's raw material is Copper
The location's raw material is Silver

buildings.name: Kremnica Mint
buildings.text: One of Europe's most respected mints, producing the famous Kremnica ducats and other coinage from Slovak gold and silver since 1328.

where.text: Gold is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Salas
buildings.text: A Vlach shepherd settlement in the Carpathian highlands, centered on seasonal sheep herding, bryndza cheese-making, and wool production.

where.text: Fur is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Carpathian Watchtower
buildings.text: A fortified observation post commanding a Carpathian mountain pass, providing early warning against raiders and channeling invaders into prepared kill zones.

buildings.name: Mining Academy
buildings.text: A technical institution modeled on the Banska Stiavnica academy, training engineers, mineralogists, and metallurgists in the latest mining sciences.

buildings.name: Tajch
buildings.text: A reservoir dammed in the hills above a mine. Its water turns the wheels that pump the shafts dry and work the stamp mills, so that the ore can be followed deeper.

children.text: The location's raw material is Silver
The location's raw material is Gold
The location's raw material is Copper
The location's raw material is Iron
The location's raw material is Lead
The location's raw material is Tin

buildings.name: Holic Majolica Works
buildings.text: A faience works on the model of the one Francis of Lorraine founded at Holic in 1743. Tin glazed tableware, painted by potters trained in the Haban tradition, is fired here for the tables of the court.

where.text: Clay is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Bergamt
buildings.text: The Royal Mining Administration: a centralized bureau overseeing mineral surveys, mining concessions, assay standards, and technical education across the Slovak mineral empire. Seated in a mining town, it raises the yield of that town's own mines.

children.text: The location's raw material is Gold
The location's raw material is Silver
The location's raw material is Copper

buildings.name: Krajina Fortress
buildings.text: A major frontier fortification commanding a strategic Carpathian approach. Built to withstand prolonged siege and house a permanent garrison of professional soldiers.

list.name: Stolica County Assembly
list.text: Inherited from the Árpádian castle-counties, the comitatus was the basic unit of Hungarian administration. A főispán appointed by the king presided over the noble assembly, but the local szlachta elected the alispán, the szolgabíró judges, and their Diet deputies. In Slovak counties the assembly was called the stolica (the seat), and each became a little republic of the local nobility, fierce in defence of its written privileges and slow to obey royal writ.

list.name: Banské Mestá Mining Towns
list.text: The seven Lower Hungarian royal mining towns (Banská Štiavnica, Kremnica, Banská Bystrica, Pukanec, Nová Baňa, Ľubietová, and Banská Belá) ran on the Schemnitzer Stadt- und Bergrecht of 1255-1466, the founding mining law of Central Europe. From 1331 the Kammergraf at Kremnica administered every mint and ore-shaft of twelve counties, and the Kremnica florin (23 carats 9 grains, struck from 1335) became the gold backbone of the Hungarian crown's revenues.

list.name: Spišská Únia
list.text: Founded by the privilege Stephen V granted the Saxon settlers in 1271 and codified in the Zipser Willkür of c. 1370 (the oldest German municipal law applied in Slovakia), the Province of XXIV Royal Spiš Towns ran its own elected diet, courts, and treasury. In 1412 Sigismund of Luxembourg pawned thirteen of the towns to Poland for 37,000 schock of Prague groschen to fund his Venetian war; they remained in Polish pledge until 1772, but the autonomous statute of the League survived intact.

list.name: Korunovačné Mesto Prešporok
list.text: When the Ottomans took Buda in 1541, Pressburg (Bratislava) became the capital of Royal Hungary. From 1536 to 1783 the city housed the chancery, the palatine's court, and the chamber of the realm; from 1542 to 1848 the Hungarian Diet sat here; and at St Martin's Cathedral nineteen Habsburg sovereigns were crowned kings and queens of Hungary between 1563 and 1830. The coronation hill projected Hungarian sovereignty from Slovak soil while Buda was Turkish.

list.name: Trnavská Synoda
list.text: When Esztergom fell to the Ottomans in 1543 the seat of the primate of Hungary was transferred to Trnava (Nagyszombat). Cardinal Péter Pázmány convened the Trnava provincial synod of 1611 to enact the Tridentine reforms, founded the University of Trnava in 1635, and reconverted most of the Hungarian magnate families to Catholicism. The Slovak lands became the institutional spine of the Hungarian Counter-Reformation, but the Lutheran burghers of the free royal towns paid the price.

list.name: Bratislavské Lýceum
list.text: The Evangelical Lyceum of Pressburg, a Lutheran seminary and gymnasium, hosted the Czech-Slav Society from 1829 and the chair where Ľudovít Štúr taught from 1837. On 2 February 1843 Štúr's circle resolved at Hlboká 5 to codify a standard Slovak literary language on the Central Slovak dialect; his Nauka reči slovenskej (1846) made the codification public and seeded the entire 1848-49 Slovak political programme. The institution forged a literate Slovak intelligentsia distinct from both the Magyar nobility and the Czech reformed clergy.
